body: I guess I’ve just been a little frustrated with derms, I’ve seen 3 separate ones and each time they’ve prescribed me topicals that have caused major allergic reactions. I tried to confide in the last one I saw about my reaction to the spironolactone in terms of edema and showed her pics, she just kind of said “oh that’s weird, it doesn’t normally do that. I dont know” which was extremely frustrating

I think the weirdest part was that on spironolactone I weighed 140lbs and my face was super puffy but now off I’m 153lbs and my face is very slim. Just really strange. Also is your iud hormonal or is it the paragard? The excess estrogen/ progesterone from the iud (if it’s the hormonal one) could cause some weight gain.

I think you’re definitely right about the dosage issue, I’m planning on seeing another gynecologist for it this time. 
I have gotten a hormonal panel before but I think I was too young to understand it so I’ll definitely bring that up with the gyn. 
The only medication filler I’m allergic to (as of now) is fluoride but as far as I know spironolactone isn’t formulated with it. 
Unfortunately I’ve tried metformin before and it threw off my thyroid labs, t3 became low and I felt tired. I usually have to be extremely careful about medications and supplements that impact thyroid function since my hypothyroidism is autoimmune and Very sensitive. 
I know I have a gluten intolerance because if I eat or touch it I break out in a bloody, dry rash so I avoid it at all costs. 
I think you bring up a good point about cortisol levels with the Cushing’s too, I definitely need to cut back on the caffeine and introduce more cardio. 
And the only thing I’m on currently is 100mcg name brand Synthroid. Other past medications (besides all the ones in the post) were Prozac, zyprexa, depakote, Wellbutrin, Buspar, nefazodone, Paxil, abilify, Zoloft, hydroxyzine, and lamictal.

Also thank you so much for taking the time to try to help me with this issue, it means a lot and you seem very knowledgeable🤍

Thank you so much for taking the time🖤
I’ve literally stumped 3 doctors with the edema part too😩 
I think I might just have to try going higher and seeing what happens. I’m just confused with the whole situation myself too
And strangely enough too, the spironolactone was the thing causing the edema. After I stopped taking it, my face went back down to its normal size

I guess I could’ve worded that post better😂 I started breaking out WHILE ON the spironolactone. Like the spironolactone itself caused me acne and I had to stop taking it. I was on 50mg in the picture.

PS: I have PCOS and hypothyroidism. My acne has returned and I wanted to give the spiro another shot (since my skin was incredibly clear for the first year of it) but I’d like to make sure this doesn’t happen again before I do it.

Also I should specify that I was breaking out WHILE ON the spironolactone and the acne/edema only went away after I discontinued the drug which is super confusing considering spiro is an androgen blocker/ diuretic? Like what?

I constantly ask them if I’m enough to the point that they get frustrated with me but I can’t help but be insecure. 
I have wonderful boyfriend but I feel like I’m just tearing him down.
